description: Recognize edge and vertex cacti by assigning each DFS fundamental cycle exclusive ownership of its edges.

source.title: Cactus Graph
source.algorithm_attribution: Iterative DFS cycle ownership identifies edge cacti; cycle vertex counts distinguish vertex cacti.
source.implementation_status: clean-room bounded scalar profile; algorithm description only

input.graph: Simple, undirected, loopless; disconnected graphs are accepted.

fields.E: 1 iff the graph is an edge cactus; otherwise 0.
fields.V: 1 iff every vertex belongs to at most one simple cycle; otherwise 0.
fields.C: Number of simple cycles when E=1; zero when E=0.

workspace.meaning: Fixed adjacency, edge ownership, DFS state, and vertex cycle-count arrays.

contract.edge_cactus: Every edge belongs to at most one simple cycle.
contract.vertex_cactus: Every vertex belongs to at most one simple cycle; a vertex cactus is also an edge cactus.
contract.primary_method: An iterative depth-first traversal finds each back-edge cycle through its parent-edge path. Reusing any tree edge rejects edge-cactus status; counting cycle vertices distinguishes vertex cacti.
contract.invalid_frames: Reject out-of-range endpoints, self-loops, duplicate undirected edges, malformed lengths, and counts outside the local bounds.

complexity.primary_time: O(N+M) for the bounded simple graph

oracle_method: The primary reference marks the fundamental cycles found by iterative DFS and rejects repeated tree-edge ownership. The independent reference computes vertex-biconnected edge blocks with Tarjan lowlinks; each non-bridge block must be one simple cycle for an edge cactus, and cycle-vertex overlap distinguishes vertex cacti.
